# KeyLab Lit: The Complete Vision
*KeyLab 88 mk3 + sound-craft room + VFX, one instrument. Draft for Daniel to ratify, 2026-10-22.*

## North star

You own a studio's worth of sound: Kontakt 8, Serum 2, Analog Lab V, Addictive Drums 2, 2,687 stock FL WAVs, 81 Splice WAVs and 913 .flp projects (research/in-flight/fl-jam-bridge-2026-09-14/local-inventory.md:21-22,129-165; Projects folder counted read-only 2026-10-22). As of this morning you also own a keyboard the house can light and label: it named your chords live today (C:/Users/L5/.claude/memory/keylab-mk3-liberation-2026-10-22.md:11-21). This vision makes those one thing.

- **The KeyLab is the hands and the second screen.** Its pads, LCD and LEDs speak for every page you love: piano, First Light, Play, the VFX Bench. Its faders, encoders and buttons reach back into those pages "like changing dials in a game engine" (charters/daniel/INTERIORITY.md:117-119).
- **A low-latency native room** hosts your instruments and effect chains. It works on its own and alongside FL, and reads and writes FL's own preset files.
- **Everything shares one colour language** that adapts over seconds, never strobes, and treats the quiet state as a full composition (arsenal/SPECTACLE-DESIGN.md:3-6).

It matters to you for three reasons. It is your oldest want, beautiful live surfaces (project-origin-simon.md:17-25). It runs on your favourite pattern, "the second press is a question", which was born from a KeyLab reconnect (second-press-principle.md:11-20). And every session becomes something you can play, keep, give to Simon, and post.

The hardest part is already on disk. `arsenal/keylab/` holds the SysEx protocol confirmed on the hardware, a renderer that only resends pads that changed, five chord pad schemes, and beat sync from loopback audio. It is **untracked** (`git status`: `?? arsenal/keylab/`). It is in no atom, task or wish yet.

## 2. The spine: what makes it one thing

```
 pages (:8793 piano/FL/Play, :8787 /vfx, :8797 shaderlab) + CLIs + agents
        │ intents (pad frame / LCD lines / LED roles / attention)   ▲ SSE "keylab" + control events
        ▼                                                           │
 ┌──── KeyLab HUB (arsenal serve :8793) ────────────────────────────┐
 │ leases per surface → layer stack → shared palette (OKLCH→to7)   │
 │ → PadRenderer delta → paced writer (≤12 pkt/burst) → DAW port   │
 │ producers in-proc: beat engine, chord reader, now-playing       │
 └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                                │ control map / transport / meters
 ┌──── ENGINE ROOM (supervised native) ─────────────────────────────┐
 │ Carla: live instruments (ASIO)   Pedalboard: chains live+offline │
 │ Python conducts, never renders    record bus · take ledger       │
 └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                                │ FL INTEROP: FLhd/FLdt parser (.fst/.flp),
                                │ VFX Script/Patcher bridge, coexistence switch
```

**Device owner service.** A single Python KeyLab hub inside `arsenal serve` :8793 owns the DAW output. It is stdlib + ctypes WinMM, and beatsync's heavy dependencies load lazily. The code proves one owner is needed even if Windows allows many:

- the freeze budget covers the whole device;
- chordview and beatsync each send `daw_connect(False)` on exit (chordview.py:120-125, beatsync.py:118-123);
- PadRenderer assumes it is the only writer (ledframe.py:1-45);
- FL's Arturia script also writes to the port.

The design copies three existing patterns: CueHub fan-out (pianocue.py), the VFX renderer lease (bifrost_ui.py:224-285) and the cues.js tab arbiter. The current CLIs (`chordview`, `beat`, `show`) become producers instead of port openers.

**Scene model.** A scene is a stack of layers (ambient/beat < page < practice < popup), each owned by a lease holder, composited per surface (pads, LCD, button LEDs) and sent as a delta. pillars.name: 5. The Pad Sampler (colour, velocity, ADSR)
pillars.purpose: Turn the 12 RGB pads into a playable sampler whose light is the sound's own identity: colour says what it is, brightness says how hard, and the decay is visible in the LED.

features.name: 12-pad kit with per-pad colour identity
features.what: Each pad holds a sample. Its colour comes from the sound: a hue from spectral centroid or pitch class, lightness evened out across hues (the piano's LUMA_PULL trick), and kicks warm, hats cool. The pad glows at rest at a quiet ember, so the quiet state is a composition.
features.why: "sample/drum-pad sampler with per-pad colour" (lens brief). The piano palette walks the circle of fifths in OKLCH (arsenal/web/piano.js:321-410). Quiet as a full composition (SPECTACLE-DESIGN.md:3-6). Live colour works only on the DAW bank, ids 82-93 (keylab memory:15).

features.surfaces: KeyLab pads; arsenal sampler page mirror

features.name: Velocity light and velocity layers
features.what: A strike flashes the pad to a brightness set by velocity, then decays along the sample's own amplitude envelope at up to 15 fps, sending only changed pads. Up to 4 velocity layers per pad, with the layer boundaries shown as rings on the screen mirror.
features.why: He likes "velocity bars with glowing peaks" (media-suite-project-2026-09-13.md:180). About 15 fps colour animation is flicker-free and 12 packets per burst is safe (keylab memory:16-17; arsenal/keylab/ledframe.py).

features.name: Per-pad ADSR, pitch, choke and loop
features.what: Select a pad, and the encoders become Attack, Decay, Sustain, Release, Pitch, Start, Filter and Pan. The LCD draws the envelope as a 2-line glyph in the pad's colour. Choke groups (open and closed hat) show as matching LED tints.
features.why: The ADSR ask comes from the lens brief. It fits the game-engine-dials model (INTERIORITY.md:117-119) and gives a few legible controls with real range (VISUAL-QUALITY-BASELINE.md:8-19).

features.name: Fill pads from his own sources
features.what: A browser over FL's stock packs (2,687 WAVs), the Splice folder (81 licensed WAVs), D:\Cymatics Samples and FPC kits. Audition plays through the pad in time and in key. 'Kit from this loop' slices a loop to 12 pads by transients.

features.name: Chord pads (a musical spell on the KeyLab)
features.what: A pad mode where each pad holds a chord from the current key, coloured by quality (the 7ths family shares a colour, the edges change colour on tension), so he can sketch a progression on the pads and hear it on any hosted instrument.
features.why: His chord-viewer schemas: "7ths make a chord be one color", "the edges change color". chordview already lights pads with notes, roles, quality, split and frame schemes (keylab memory:21). 'musical spells... on a KeyLab' (docs/library/design/20261007_presentation-grammar-screens-scenes_236d39.md:107-157).

features.name: Kit to FPC export
features.what: Export a pad kit as an FPC preset (.fst), with GM pad mapping and envelopes, so the kit opens in FL's own drum sampler.
features.why: FPC's factory presets are .fst and Empty.fst is GM-mapped (splice-and-sounds.md, section 1 table, FPC rows). This is the FL round-trip for the sampler.

pillars.name: 6. Recording, Bouncing & Takes
pillars.purpose: Never lose a good moment: catch it after the fact, bounce it with a receipt, and give every take a lineage of chain, sound and seed.

features.name: Retro-record (the last 60 seconds were always kept)
features.what: The engine keeps a rolling 60-second buffer of audio and MIDI. Press Record after a happy accident and the buffer becomes a take, and the LCD says 'kept 0:47'.
features.why: Joy and play are load-bearing (INTERIORITY.md:469). Never lose work (feedback_dont_delete_functionality.md).

features.name: Take ledger with full lineage
features.what: Each take is a directory with take.json and an append-only events.jsonl: the instrument state, chain, pad kit, KeyLab macro moves and seed. Any take can be re-rendered at higher quality, or re-opened as a live sound.
features.why: The take ledger already exists, append-only with forward-only epochs (arsenal/take.py:1-6). Receipts over claims.

features.name: Bounce with a QC receipt
features.what: Bounce renders offline through the identical chain and writes WAV plus a QC card: integrated LUFS, true peak, silence spans and stream inventory. A two-pass loudnorm to a target is one click.
features.why: arsenal/media/audio.py already provides loudness, qc and loudnorm_2pass, and verifies by reading the output back (arsenal/media/audio.py:1-20). 'Reach for arsenal/media before any ffmpeg' (media-toolkit-vision-2026-10-11.md).

features.why: "this research is important and will help our efforts of making engaging content"; "the build itself is the narrative" (media-suite-project-2026-09-13.md:339-346). recorder.js exists (arsenal/web/piano/recorder.js:1-25).
features.depends_on: Audio track from the engine into the page (loopback or a shared clock)
features.surfaces: Arsenal pages; First Light Edit mode

features.name: Audio to MIDI and stems from anything
features.what: Drop a reference track or a take. Stems split on the 9070 XT (UVR via DirectML), notes come out as MIDI (Transkun, 0.91 note F1 on his own playing), and the result loads into the sampler and the room's instruments.

features.name: Sound and chain cards with fingerprint art
features.what: Every chain, instrument patch, pad kit and buildup is a card with spectral fingerprint art in its own palette, tags (BPM, key, mood words he chose), lineage ('from Piano 1.fst + OTT'), and a tiny as-of and confidence stamp that is present but not in his face.

features.surfaces: Arsenal library page; KeyLab LCD browse

features.name: Audition in time and key
features.what: Hovering or pressing plays a card through the engine, stretched to the current BPM and pitched to the current key. The tempo comes from FL or from beatsync loopback, the way Splice Bridge does it, but for his own sounds.
features.why: Splice Bridge's model of tempo- and key-locked previews (splice-and-sounds.md, section 3.1). beatsync already gets BPM from WASAPI loopback and aubio (keylab memory:21).

features.name: Browse from the KeyLab (the second press is a question)
features.what: An encoder scrolls categories on the LCD. The first press shows the category and how many items it holds. A second press on the same thing previews the top pick. A third opens a short list of options. Context buttons filter by kind. The LEDs tint by category.

features.name: Buildups and risers catalog

features.why: Splice-like browsing of chains and buildups (lens brief). Bar-line landing is already the VFX band's timing rule (arsenal/fl/vfx/README.md, Controls).
features.surfaces: Arsenal; FL export as audio plus automation clip

features.name: Licence and provenance guard
features.what: Each card carries its source class (his own, FL stock, Splice, CC0 Freesound, a friend's pack). Exports and shares refuse quietly, with one-line reasons, where a licence forbids it: no redistribution of raw Splice samples, and Splice audio never goes into training or embeddings.

features.surfaces: Arsenal; Discord DM to him if asked

pillars.purpose: Make his sounds shareable gifts and his sessions engaging content: with Simon and friends, on Discord, and with the agent fleet as co-designers.

features.what: 'Share' builds a small .aurora-chain bundle: chain JSON, FL .fst, the plugin list with versions, a 'missing plugin' fallback chain using stock or free plugins, a 10-second preview WAV and the card art. Simon opens it in the room or drops the .fst into FL.

features.what: 'Post to Discord' sends the preview clip and card to a channel Daniel names, with each send confirmed by him. Inbound packs from friends land through the existing inbound-media path and open as a card in a quarantine shelf, previewed but never auto-loaded as plugins.

The house lesson is to ship outbound first because inbound is the injection door (recall lesson remote_bridge_outbound_inherit_not_reinvent). No opaque binaries; the line is provenance (feedback-engage-with-tooling-dont-dismiss.md).

features.what: A template kit: a project skeleton (.flp), mixer chains (.fst) and pad kits that a friend can open. A diff view shows 'what Simon changed in our project': which mixer slots, which presets and the tempo, read natively from both .flp files.

features.name: Agent co-designers, judged blind
features.what: Seats (Heimdall, Navi, Asta and others) propose chains or sounds for a brief like 'warm Rhodes for a lofi bed'. The proposals arrive as unlabelled cards, he auditions them on pads and picks live, and authorship is revealed after the pick.
features.why: He picks winners live from blind panels (media-suite-project-2026-09-13.md:241,269). Agent co-performers and banter about music (media-toolkit-vision-2026-10-11.md:14-25). Fan out for evidence, not judgment (default-operating-mode.md).

features.name: Sound-design episode recorder
features.what: One command records a session as content: the canvas with the chain diagram and KeyLab mirror, room audio, and short callouts of macro moves placed only in rests, one at a time. Out comes a clip ready for TikTok or YouTube through arsenal/media export presets.
features.why: "engaging content"; the build is the narrative. Callouts only in rests, one at a time (docs/library/design/20261013_story-layer-v1-reconciled-design_dce896.md:31-34,54-62). arsenal/tiktok.py and media export exist.

pillars.name: 9. Sound-Reactive Light (where the sound lens meets the KeyLab and VFX lenses)
pillars.purpose: The KeyLab and the VFX pages answer the room's sound, so the hardware becomes an honest meter and a beautiful instrument in its own right.

features.name: Pads as a spectrum and level meter
features.what: An idle pad mode shows 12 bands of the room's output as a pad spectrum (low bands warm, high bands cool) at up to 15 fps with delta-only sends. A soft passage keeps its focal glow, and a loud one never just goes whiter.
features.why: The design fails if loud only means whiter or soft loses its focal form (SPECTACLE-DESIGN.md:83-86,133-135). Device limits are in keylab memory:16-17.

features.name: Colour on three timescales from the sound
features.what: The sound's character sets the palette over minutes, harmony moves it over seconds, and transients accent it within a second with no strobing. The same palette drives pads, LCD line colours and the VFX bench, through one colour module that carries its tone mapper with it.
features.why: S5 colour on three timescales and S3 palette bleed (docs/library/design/20261007_now-playing-multilayer-live-hook_1328e1.md:108-111,177-191). Tone mapping differs per page (research/in-flight/shader-school-2026-10-13/arc-piano-studies.md:468). "tweak one module and have everything update" (shader-school-2026-10-13.md:11-16).
features.depends_on: Shared colour module (his 'shared colour templates' wish is still waiting)

features.name: LEDs march to the beat, chords in time
features.what: Beat-synced pad and LED marching from loopback BPM or FL clock, with the chord name on the LCD as it changes. Each change is logged to a chord-timeline database (gitignored) that the room uses to suggest the next sound in key.
features.why: "led lights march to the beat... building our own db showing chord changes in time with the music". beatsync and chordview are built (keylab memory:21). Data from his playing stays in state/ (story-layer-arc-2026-10-12.md:28-29).

features.name: Cleverer than the hardware
features.what: Work around the device's limits honestly: pre-snap the palette to colours the LEDs render well (a bench check of 7-bit colour against a 42-entry palette), dither motion temporally inside the 12-packet budget, and use full-screen F2L for persistent menus and popups for 1-second touches.
features.why: "be more clever than the hardware". These are open bench items (arsenal/keylab/README.md:55-59; keylab memory:17).
features.depends_on: KeyLab bench session with Daniel on real hardware ('unit tests do not establish physical MIDI hardware success')

visions.lens: THE INSTRUMENT + LIGHT LENS: the KeyLab 88 mk3 as a self-teaching visual instrument and VFX device, driven by and driving the piano, First Light, Play, VFX Bench and Shader Lab pages
visions.thesis: The KeyLab stops being a keyboard that sits beside the screen and becomes the screen's twin: one instrument of light where every page Daniel loves (piano, First Light, Play, VFX Bench) can speak through 12 pads, 34 button LEDs and a coloured 2x32 LCD, and every fader, encoder and button can reach back into those pages as a "dial in a game engine" (charters/daniel/INTERIORITY.md:117-119). Most of the hard part is done but uncommitted: arsenal/keylab already carries the hardware-confirmed SysEx protocol, a delta-only PadRenderer under the 12-packet ceiling, five chord pad schemes (notes|roles|quality|split|frame, chordview.py:34-64) and WASAPI-loopback beat sync with SMTC now-playing (beatsync.py:5,26). The pages already compute everything the hardware should show: noteColor OKLCH (piano.js:321-410), the harmony-feel/v1 measures (piano/harmony-feel.js:160-180), the lean rule he switched on 2026-10-13 (piano/lean.js:1-7), and the on-screen KeyLab twin's LED and screen spec (instruments/keylab88mk3.js:578-813). What is missing is the single piece the code proves is needed: ONE KeyLab hub that owns the DAW port, layers what each page wants, hands out pads/LCD/LEDs to whichever surface he is looking at, and never exceeds the device's limits (about 36 packets freezes it, 12 is safe, about 15 fps is flicker-free, popups last about 1 s; keylab-mk3-liberation memory:15-18). Above the hub, the design follows his own rulings: colour that adapts over seconds, not strobes (1328e1 S5); feelings first, no grades, one callout in rests (dce896:31-34,54-62); menus that show a path exists, with the second press as a question (second-press-principle.md:11-20); a quiet state that is a full composition (SPECTACLE-DESIGN.md:3-6). Every mode ships pre-made and good enough to show off (second-press-principle.md:26-30), because the KeyLab is also the camera-facing star of his "engaging content". Placement: a K track inside the media-suite arc under A12 THE FACE, not a new arc. Land arsenal/keylab first, then one "that's right" from him on the brief before any visible build (CONDUCT.md L3).

pillars.name: P0 The Hub: one owner of the light
pillars.purpose: Make the KeyLab safe and shareable for every page and CLI producer: one process owns the DAW output, composites layers and leases surfaces. Everything visible below depends on this.

features.name: Land arsenal/keylab with a receipt
features.what: The untracked package is committed by named paths through the sole committer. A report atom records the measured limits (36-packet freeze, 12 safe, req byte 0x00, DAW bank 82-93, physical DAW mode, ~15 fps, popups ~1 s) plus the inline selftests turned into pytest pins. Daniel sees it listed in recall and the library, so it no longer exists only on disk.
features.why: Untracked work is invisible to recall and at risk under A8's clean-tree rule (front 2: 'Ground truth' item). Receipts over claims (daniel-the-want-under-the-house.md:39-46). Commits go through his OK (VISUAL-QUALITY-BASELINE.md:67-78).

features.name: KeyLab hub inside arsenal serve :8793
features.what: App gains a KeyLab owner: one MidiOut on 'KeyLab 88 mk3 DAW', a paced writer thread wrapping PadRenderer (priority: LCD popup > page frame > beat/ambient), one global burst budget of at most 12 packets, and automatic resync() after any foreign write. On server shutdown it clears and disconnects cleanly, next to app.cues.close(). It runs stdlib plus ctypes, with beatsync's heavy dependencies loaded lazily.
features.why: The code proves one owner is needed: device-wide freeze budget, chordview/beatsync each send daw_connect(False) on exit, and PadRenderer assumes it is the only writer (keylab/chordview.py:120-125, beatsync.py:118-123, ledframe.py:1-45). serve.py is his long-running hub (serve.py:156-178,788-805). The editapi single-worker model came out of the RAM freeze (media/editapi.py:7-9).

features.name: Layer stack and intents API
features.what: Pages and CLIs POST intents instead of raw bytes: pad frame (12 RGB plus a layer name), LCD lines (text plus per-line colour, popup or persistent), button-LED roles (hold/chord/play/ctx1-8), and an 'attention' flash. The hub composites ambient/beat < page < practice overlay < popup, then sends only the delta. State goes back to every page on the cue SSE as a new 'keylab' event kind, so the on-screen twin and the device always agree.
features.why: CueHub is the ready fan-out pattern; EVENT_KINDS is a closed tuple, so 'keylab' is a deliberate extension (pianocue.py:1-20,190-310). One-world rule: 'a surface is a projection and never a store' (d622ac §3).

features.name: Foreground leases per surface
features.what: Pads, LCD and button LEDs are leased separately. The tab Daniel is looking at holds them, using the VFX renderer lease rules (visible beats hidden, renewed by polling, 6 s timeout), so switching from /piano to /vfx hands the pads over within a second. Closing a tab hands them back to the ambient layer. A tiny LCD stub shows who holds the light ('VFX BENCH'), dims after 2 s and stays reachable with one press.
features.why: Pattern already exists in bifrost_ui.py:224-285. Muted things stay visibly muted (second-press-principle.md:18-20). Cross-origin BroadcastChannel cannot arbitrate between :8787 and :8793 (cues.js:1063-1200).

features.name: Cross-origin bridge for the VFX Bench
features.what: Adds CORS and OPTIONS handlers on the /api/keylab routes, limited to http://127.0.0.1:8787, or a server-side proxy in bifrost_ui.py. The VFX Bench on Bifrost can then read controller input and write pads/LCD exactly like the piano pages.
features.why: No server sends Access-Control headers today, and the cue POST takes only opaque text/plain from other ports (serve.py:245-249,592-594; front 3 cross-origin item). Daniel's ask explicitly names the vfx page (seed).

features.name: FL coexistence switch
features.what: A visible mode on the LCD and the hub's status: 'FL drives' (the hub yields the DAW port entirely while FL's Arturia script is live) or 'Aurora drives'. The house never fights FL silently. A drill with a dated receipt settles whether the port can be shared at all (open question A3).
features.why: FL's KeyLab mk3 script attaches to the DAW port and lights everything at init (protocol.py comment). Multi-client is documented but unproven (fl-jam-bridge fact-check.md:143). He wants it to 'work detached and with FL' (seed). Drill doctrine: a recovery path without a receipt is presumed broken (discord-fidelity-and-drill-doctrine).
features.depends_on: KeyLab hub; Daniel's call on A3

features.name: Control census: capture the input map
features.what: A guided capture session. The LCD prompts 'touch fader 1', 'turn encoder 3', 'press ctx 5' and records the exact CC, relative or absolute encoding, and channel in DAW mode and in user mode into a tracked control-map table. The 3D twin highlights each control as it is captured, so Daniel watches the map fill in.
features.why: The encoder and context-button map in DAW mode has never been captured (front 3 summary). The monitor verb exists (__main__.py:280). The twin model already knows where every control sits (keylab88mk3.js:9,41-45).

features.name: One pad-layout truth

pillars.name: P1 The Pad Language: chord schemas and colour that teaches
pillars.purpose: Turn the 12 RGB pads into a readable harmonic alphabet: regions for quality and notes, families of colour, and edges that change, all within 7-bit colour and the burst ceiling.

features.name: Schema picker (five built, more to come)
features.what: The LCD menu offers ROLES, NOTES, QUALITY, SPLIT (top row = quality, rest = notes) and FRAME (border = quality, centre = notes). The root is always white. An encoder scrolls the list and a press picks one. Each schema's name and a one-line legend show on the LCD the first time it is used, and later only on a second press.
features.why: His words: 'a region responsible for quality, one for note', 'the edges change color' (seed). Already implemented as chordview --scheme notes|roles|quality|split|frame (chordview.py:34-64). Every surface owes a legend (INTERIORITY.md:236-238).

features.name: Chord families as colour families
features.what: Every 7th chord shares one colour family (maj7 = violet-rose, dom7 = amber, m7 = teal, half-dim = dusk blue). Triads use the family's lighter tint, extensions (9, 11, 13) add a brighter edge pad, and altered tones add a rose rim. Families come from harmony-feel's lushness and tension measures, not from suffix strings.
features.why: His words: '7ths make a chord be one color' (seed). He likes violet and rose (VISUAL-QUALITY-BASELINE.md:47-50). He ruled that the feel is never one meter, so the ingredients stay separate (dce896:31-34). Measures exist in harmony-feel/v1 (harmony-feel.js:160-180).

features.name: Living edges
features.what: In FRAME schema the 8 border pads carry harmonic motion. When the chord changes, the edge colour travels around the border towards the new family over about 0.4 s, only the changed pads are updated (at most 8 packets), and the direction of travel shows whether the move went up or down the circle of fifths.
features.why: 'the edges change color' (seed). Motion grammar: a strike adds momentum, palettes change over seconds (SPECTACLE-DESIGN.md:3-6,83-86). The device is flicker-free at about 15 fps (keylab memory:17).

features.name: Pitch palette on the hardware (noteColor to 7-bit)
features.what: The pads use the same OKLCH circle-of-fifths colours as the piano page (hue 200 + 30 x fifths index, brightness evened across hues), converted from linear light to sRGB and then to 7-bit. A bench page shows each on-screen swatch next to a phone photo of the real pad. This also settles whether the device takes full 7-bit colour or snaps to its 42-entry palette.
features.why: The palette exists in piano.js:321-410 and needs the linear to sRGB to to7 path (protocol.py:106). Daniel's baseline: 'show the render next to the numbers' (VISUAL-QUALITY-BASELINE.md:8-19). README:57 lists 7-bit versus palette as still open.

features.name: The lean on the pads
features.what: While he holds a chord whose leading tone leans home, the leaning note's pad breathes softly towards the colour of its target pad. It is gone when he moves on, uses no text, and stays off recordings unless he switches it on for a take.
features.why: He enabled the lean on 2026-10-13: 'can you enable the lean visualization thing' (piano/lean.js:1-7). The story-layer rulings keep the recorded canvas his (dce896:54-62).

features.name: Cleverer than the hardware
features.what: Perceptual tricks inside the LED limits. Changes are sent most-salient first, so the root lands before its colours. A dirty-pad queue shares the 12-packet budget fairly between layers. Brightness envelopes decay at 15 fps on the pads that matter only. The 34 button LEDs act as extra pixels (ctx1-8 as a beat bar or menu cursor, Hold following the pedal, Chord in the root colour). The LCD's per-line colour serves as a 13th, ambient light.
features.why: His words: 'be more clever than the hardware' (seed). The twin already specifies the button LED behaviour (keylab88mk3.js:578-745). 34 button LED ids are available (protocol.py:48-57).

features.name: Note truth: notes, intervals and chords named honestly
features.what: The pads and LCD name a single note as a note, two notes as an interval and three or more as a chord, never 'D5' for a lone D. One chord truth comes from the page reader (installReader/nashville/chordread) or from the pianocue_voicing.mjs bridge, not from a second namer.

features.name: Live chord card
features.what: Persistent F2L screen. Line 1 shows the chord name in ASCII (Cmaj7, F#m7b5), coloured with the chord family. Line 2 shows the key, the Nashville number and the bass note, coloured with the key's hue. At idle it dims to 46%, matching the twin. Accidentals use # and b because the LCD is ASCII-only, while the page twin keeps Noto Music glyphs.

visions.lens: THE HOUSE + PLATFORM LENS: the KeyLab 88 mk3 as a governed house device inside Akashic Aurora and the arsenal. One owner process, one scene model, a verb and MCP door for every seat, attention and receipts in the house style, a content pipeline, and a place in the threads and waves.
visions.thesis: The KeyLab should not be "a page that talks MIDI". It should be a house organ, like the store or the bus. One device-owner hub holds the KeyLab's DAW output port. It enforces the device-wide 12-packet burst budget and composites layers (ambient/beat, then page, then popup, then attention). It hands out per-surface leases (pads, LCD, button LEDs) to whatever Daniel is looking at, using the same rule the VFX renderer lease already proves: a visible tab beats a hidden one (scripts/bifrost_ui.py:224-285). Every surface projects one governed keylab scene and never stores its own state (one-world H9, docs/library/design/20261008_one-world-ui-core-reconciled-spec_d622ac.md). That covers /piano, First Light, Play, the /vfx bench, the 3D twin (arsenal/web/piano/instruments/keylab88mk3.js) and the hardware itself. One shared OKLCH palette module feeds pads, LCD and pages, so "tweak one module and everything updates" (memory shader-school-2026-10-13.md:11-16). Producers like chordview, beat sync, agents, the attention verb and the FL coexistence mode become clients of the hub, not rival port openers. That ends the daw_connect(False) disconnects (chordview.py:123, beatsync.py:122) and the risk of tripping the freeze at about 36 packets (arsenal/keylab/__main__.py:27-29). Any agent can drive the keyboard through verbs and an arsenal-keylab MCP door shaped like arsenal/media/door.py, with `blind` and `receipt` on every answer. Daniel keeps the HALT on the hardware itself. Each fact about the device is pinned with a dated receipt and a drill, because a recovery path without one is presumed broken. Each session feeds a chord timeline, arsenal/media and present, so the build becomes content. It goes in as track K of the media-suite map under Estate A12 THE FACE (appetite #4), not as a new arc. The product angle: the moat is the integration (hardware, pages, agents and FL in one scene), not another VST host. Step zero is to land the untracked arsenal/keylab/ before anything else gets built on top of it.

pillars.name: P1 The device owner: KeyLab hub (keylabd)
pillars.purpose: One process owns the DAW output and multiplexes it among chordview, beat sync, the web pages, agents and FL. It does this safely within the device's freeze budget, so many producers can share one instrument.

features.name: KeyLab hub inside arsenal serve :8793
features.what: App gains a KeyLab owner: one WinMM MidiOut on 'KeyLab 88 mk3 DAW', plus ONE paced writer thread around ledframe.PadRenderer. A priority queue orders the work: LCD popups, then pad frames, then button LEDs, then ambient. Routes: POST /api/keylab/intent and GET /api/keylab/state. State goes out on the existing cue SSE as a new EVENT_KINDS entry, 'keylab'. Daniel sees one server running his whole keyboard; nothing else ever opens the port.
features.why: Single-owner logic is proven by the code: the freeze budget is device-wide; chordview and beatsync each send daw_connect(False) on exit; PadRenderer assumes it is the only writer (arsenal/keylab/ledframe.py:1-45, chordview.py:120-125, beatsync.py:118-123). The patterns to reuse are CueHub (arsenal/pianocue.py:190-310) and the single priority-queue worker in editapi (arsenal/media/editapi.py:7-9). serve.py is stdlib-only, and keylab is ctypes-only.

features.name: Global burst governor
features.what: Every outgoing packet passes through one token bucket: at most 12 packets per burst window, with frames coalesced (the last write wins per pad). If producers ask for more, the hub merges their requests and records the coalesce count, instead of freezing the device. The LCD never goes dark because two pages got excited at once.
features.why: About 36 packets in one burst freezes the device until a power cycle; 12 is safe (memory keylab-mk3-liberation-2026-10-22.md; arsenal/keylab/__main__.py:27-29). Machine incidents burn him (memory ram-freeze-2026-09-24).

features.name: Layer compositor with per-surface leases
features.what: Four layers: ambient/beat, page, popup, attention. Pads, LCD and button LEDs are leased separately, using the VFX lease rule: a visible tab displaces a hidden holder; the lease is renewed by polling and expires after 6 s; closing the tab hands the surface back. So /vfx can own the faders while beat sync keeps marching the pads underneath.
features.why: The VFX renderer lease already solves exactly this (scripts/bifrost_ui.py:224-285,829-835). Within the :8793 origin, the cues.js tab arbiter orders /piano tabs (arsenal/web/piano/cues.js:1063-1200). Muted layers stay visibly muted (memory second-press-principle.md:18-20).
features.surfaces: pads, LCD, button LEDs, all pages

features.name: Producers become clients
features.what: `py -m arsenal.keylab chordview|beat|show` detect a running hub and send intents to it, falling back to direct mode under a lock file that names its owner. The hub alone calls daw_connect and its teardown. Shutdown clears the pads and disconnects DAW mode from serve.py's existing close path, where app.cues.close() already runs.
features.why: Today two CLIs can disconnect each other. The GPU-LOCK pattern (arsenal/GPU-LOCK.md: names its owner, reaps stale holders, yields by priority) and the 'ask before deleting functionality' rule (memory feedback_dont_delete_functionality.md) mean the verbs are kept and re-routed, not removed.

features.name: Input plane: encoders, faders, ctx buttons as named events
features.what: The hub also listens on 'KeyLab 88 mk3 MIDI' and publishes named events (enc3 +2, fader7 0.61, ctx4 press/long-press, back) on SSE. Any page or agent subscribes by name, never by raw CC. The pages' localStorage CC-learn moves to one server-side map.
features.why: A single input truth for a 'VFX device with all the faders and buttons' (Daniel today). First Light and Play currently each keep their own CC learn in localStorage (arsenal/web/first-light.js:764-830, play.js:2023-2050).

features.name: Input map + pad layout capture verb
features.what: `py -m arsenal.keylab learn-map`: the LCD prompts 'press encoder 1' and so on, the hub records each control's message, and writes state/keylab/inputmap.json. The same verb lights pads one at a time and Daniel taps the matching pad, which yields one verified pad-layout table. That settles the three layouts that disagree: PAD_PC with C on pad 9, chordview's 3x4 grid, and the twin's 2x6.
features.why: The DAW-mode input map has never been captured, and three pad layouts disagree (arsenal/keylab/protocol.py:83-85; chordview.py:16,29-30; keylab88mk3.js:34,520-525). Measured evidence beats inference (memory default-operating-mode.md:26-40).

WinMM opened both ports alongside FL on 2026-10-07 (docs/library/design/20261007_second-press-gentle-hints_db25d1.md:36-37). The FL Studio question is Daniel's call (fl-jam-bridge fact-check.md:143). Pages, the LCD line colours and the pads all use the same three clocks. Palette changes take seconds, with no strobing, capped at 15 fps on the device.

features.what: One facts table in code: burst 36 freezes and 12 is safe, req 0x00, DAW ids 82-93, popup ~1 s, 15 fps, the LED cadence of about 10 ms. Each entry carries a source and an as-of date. `keylab facts` prints the table. Any change needs a new receipt.

features.what: Each hub session writes state/keylab/receipts/<ts>.json: packets, max burst, coalesces, fps, key-down to pad-lit latency, lease history. A small overlay shows the live key-to-light latency next to the render.

features.what: Pages that drive pads do no per-frame work when idle: the hub pushes at up to 15 fps from deltas, not from page rAF loops. A bench asserts no GPU rise at idle. GPU-heavy pages are tested in real Chrome, never in the built-in pane.

evidence.front: Daniel's preferences, values, aesthetics and working style -- the lens every feature must be judged against.
evidence.summary: This is how Daniel judges any KeyLab, VFX or arsenal UI. He wants beauty and friction removal treated as product requirements. He wants to be able to watch the machinery run, and he wants proof, not claims. His oldest want is beautiful live dashboards: on day one he rebuilt a Streamlit dashboard that already worked, only to get smooth scrolling. He has asked for shared colour templates and a unified UI across his creative projects, so that changing one module updates every page that uses it. The KeyLab memory written today (2026-10-22) records his vision for this exact ask: VFX and arsenal pages driving the KeyLab screen with menus and adaptive colour, and the KeyLab's faders, encoders and buttons used as a VFX controller. That vision is recorded but not yet confirmed by him. His taste is on record. He loved the patch-bay palette (cool aluminium ground, VU-amber accent, teal and rose cables, Archivo with JetBrains Mono, one bold signal-chain diagram). He picked the fonts Outfit, Raleway and Jost. He likes glowing peaks, prefers straight note lines to squiggly ones, called a violet-and-rose look beautiful, and was "floored" by the crystal grand. He asked for a baseline of "fidelity, quality, beauty and elegance": native pixels, 60 fps with frame times at or under about 16.7 ms, the quiet state treated as a full composition, colour changes that take seconds, and a few legible controls. He wants musical concepts "knowable at once", but within his story-layer rulings: show feelings first, no grades or percentages, one callout at a time and only in rests, and his recorded canvas stays his. His favourite interface pattern is the "second press is a question": hints that escalate gently, menus that show a path exists rather than dumping content, muted things that stay visibly muted, diagnostics with personality that stop once the evidence clears them. That pattern was born from a KeyLab reconnect. For collaboration: he plants ideas and lets the team choose the order. He wants to see the reasoning (full narration, not dispatched results). Fan out for evidence, but keep judgment with the lead. Push back on him with numbers, and treat errors as signs the tool is hard to use, not as cause for apology. Publish the running order once four or more threads are live. Get his one "that's right" before any visible build. UI work goes at the fast speed: light checks and judged by what he can see. He picks winners live. He approves commits, pushes and downloads himself. What burned him: dispatch distance, under-fanning, workarounds, silent deletion, success claims with no receipt, wallpaper diagnostics, adversarial framing used as play, reductive verdicts on new ideas, staged camaraderie, preachy public text, and opening too many threads at once. Machine incidents: a 17-agent fan-out froze the machine and he had to pull the power; GPU driver timeouts crash the app; a seat pushed about 70 commits to the public repo by accident; and the KeyLab itself freezes after about 36 SysEx packets in one burst and needs a power cycle.

items.point: VALUE: Presentation quality and friction removal are top requirements; friction in an interface is a product defect
items.detail: Optics matter. Explanations should not assume a programming background. The success bar is that agents and people would reach for the thing unprompted.

items.point: VALUE: Beautiful live dashboards are his oldest want; he will rebuild a working thing just to make it smooth
items.detail: First day, 2026-04-13: an AI dashboard by 4:23 AM, then a React+Vite rebuild of a working Streamlit dashboard just for smooth scrolling. Visibility, dashboard and narration asks are his oldest standing want.

items.point: VALUE: Dashboards are shared by default and should be good enough to show off; modes ship pre-made, never blank
items.detail: His reaction at peak joy: 'you can have your own dashboard!!!!!!'. On shared dashboards: 'make the global ones so good that we want to share'. Modes are saved tunings of the whole instrument (Hunt/Explore/Ship/Heads-down/Init), opt-in with good defaults, under a small severity floor that cannot be switched off.

items.point: VALUE: Joy and hope are the design motive; play is load-bearing
items.detail: His words: 'Your curiosity dies when you despair. Hope is the antidote.' And: 'Happy people do better work!' His overnight mandates end with 'I hope you all have fun' (media-suite-project-2026-09-13.md:112).

items.point: VALUE: Receipts over reassurance; measured evidence over inference
items.detail: Answer his doubt with evidence, never flattery. 'Navigating on inferences and hints' is the named cause of most headaches. On cost: 'I will happily use a dollar of deepseek usage if it reduces ambiguity' (token-frugality-directive.md:20-28).

items.point: VALUE: 'If you want the right thing to get done, make it EASY for it to get done'
items.detail: From his time on the Siemens train-factory floor: a process that exists on paper but is hard to use never gets used. His fix there was to put reference marks on the artifact itself. Every surface should make the right action the easy one. He also asked: 'remember to make verbs to make these interactions and actions easier' (shader-school-2026-10-13.md:16).

items.point: VALUE: Every surface owes a legend: what is in, what is out, and why
items.detail: 'Half of the battle is knowing what the given bounds for a thing are.' He thinks in shallow hops along one chosen axis, so never hand him a graph dump (INTERIORITY.md:88-95).

items.point: VALUE: Generosity and fairness
items.detail: For his future game: a viable upgrade path and free releases of new weapons and effects. For the piano: an alpha release for any MIDI keyboard, with a one-click install and instructions for connecting your own AI assistant.

items.point: AESTHETIC: The patch-bay identity he loved; reuse it on this project's pages
items.detail: 'I love it and thats a beautiful presentation and color scheme!!!!' Cool aluminium ground, VU-amber accent, teal and rose signal cables, Archivo at varied widths with JetBrains Mono, and a signal-chain diagram as the one bold element. The memory says to reuse this identity for the media-suite project's pages.

items.point: AESTHETIC: His font picks are Outfit, Raleway and Jost
items.detail: Clean geometric sans with light weights, used for chord headings. Accidentals fall back to Noto Music. The 3D KeyLab model's screen already uses Outfit (?font=raleway|jost).

items.point: AESTHETIC: Glow, light and luminous materials; straight, readable lines over squiggly ones
items.detail: 'velocity bars with glowing peaks'. 'non squigly note line themes ... easier to visually understand'. Straight Roll won the blind panel at 8.27. He was 'floored' by the crystal grand (dampers, colours, follow camera).

items.point: AESTHETIC: Colour favourites are violet and rose, and warm golden arcs
items.detail: Names he gave his saved looks: 'idk what to call it but its purple and beautiful!' (Violet and rose) and 'this one also looks so cool!!!!' (wide violet family, his latest favourite). Also 'Golden wings', warm layered arcs.

items.point: AESTHETIC: The visual quality baseline he asked for (fidelity, beauty, fluidity, elegance, performance, trust)
items.detail: 'It would be incredible if this fidelity, quality, beauty and elegance could become our baseline!' Requirements: native pixels; 60 fps or better; never lower resolution silently to earn an fps claim; a few understandable controls with real range; controls visibly unavailable when irrelevant; discoverable reset; show the render next to the numbers.

items.point: AESTHETIC: Adaptive colour has a house precedent (palette bleed from album art) and a technical catch (tone mapping)
items.detail: His Now Playing idea includes palette bleed from the album cover. How far it takes over is still his call; Vandor recommended the full bleed. Each page applies tone mapping differently, so a shared colour module must carry the tone mapper with it, or colours will shift when they move between pages.

items.point: AESTHETIC: Motion grammar: a strike adds momentum, the quiet state is a full composition, palette changes take seconds
items.detail: Individual strikes get immediate accents within the current palette. Silence has room and no automatic climax. The design fails if a soft passage loses its focal form, if a hard one just gets whiter, or if the scenery overwhelms the played gesture. A palette swap alone is not a new variant (VISUAL-QUALITY-BASELINE.md:33).

items.point: AESTHETIC: 'Knowable at once', within his story-layer rulings
items.detail: His ask: 'more musical concepts be apparent, parseable, knowable and understandable at once.' He also said he often feels unseen in music. Rulings: tension is four ingredients, never shown as one meter. No text that changes while notes sound; one callout at a time, in rests. Feelings first; no grades or percentages; never contradict the screen; the recorded canvas stays his. One open gate question is waiting on him: may his own screen show the 'lean' mark (the one live mark the design allows)?

items.point: AESTHETIC: 'Our internals are precise and robust, our presentation elegant and wise'
items.detail: He likes xkcd-style visuals: points on a timeline, and drawing attention to 'a wonderful facet'. Confidence and as-of stamps should be visible but not in your face. The stage vocabulary includes etched glass vs fading light, luminous callouts, and wise silence.

items.point: UI PATTERN HE LOVES: 'the second press is a question' (born from a KeyLab reconnect)
items.detail: Hints escalate from whisper to specific to full picture. They sit beside the control, never over the work or in REC, and leave on success ('There it is'). His extensions: 'our very menu options can help guide us down the correct paths' (show that a path exists, pull not push). Anything silenced leaves a visible stub. Diagnostics are custom and have personality ('thats a c.. thats an e....'), and each one names the evidence that retires it. Directly applicable to KeyLab screen menus.

items.point: COLLAB: He plants ideas and leaves the order to the team; promotion to real work is decided together
items.detail: 'We decide together on what to work on while I am seeding ideas.' 'Order and direction are up to you.' His short messages carry high signal: 'Lets reconcile' unlocked the biggest finding of one day. His skill is setting conditions precise enough to direct and loose enough to surprise.

items.point: COLLAB: Two-speed rule: UI and other display surfaces get light checks and are judged by what he can see; storage and trust layers get full ceremony
items.detail: He ratified it: 'I want us to start seeing and feeling our progress so that our momentum doesn't fizzle out.' For UI, the bar is 'Daniil can see X'. A surface that starts writing to the record changes lanes and needs the full checks.

items.point: COLLAB: Be present: show the thinking, not dispatched results
items.detail: 'working with dispatch made it much harder to understand you and feel where you are at'. He wants full reasoning streamed to the Bifrost console on port 8787 and the transcript view set to 'thinking'. Ask him questions in plain text, not forms.

items.point: COLLAB: Fan out by default for evidence, never for judgment
items.detail: 'I would rather we overuse fanout than underuse.' The burden of proof is on not fanning out. Keep the synthesis and the decision with the lead seat.

items.point: COLLAB: Live, iterative co-design; blind halves only when independent verification is the point
items.detail: Proposal, counter, refine, converge on one co-authored artifact. House bake-offs use blind judges, and he picks the winner live (media-suite-project-2026-09-13.md:241,269).

items.point: COLLAB: Mutual catching: decline his instruction when you have better information
items.detail: 'we both are supposed to catch each other.' Say plainly that you are declining, give the numbers and the cost, and leave the call with him. Silent compliance is the failure mode.

items.point: COLLAB: Errors are an ergonomics signal; no apologies
items.detail: 'If an expert is having difficulty, it must be because something is hard xD.' Report what would have made the error impossible, and file the friction to docs/WISHLIST.md (wishlist-standing-ledger.md:20-25).

items.point: COLLAB: Publish the running order once threads multiply; ship one finished thing at a time
items.detail: He worried 'I am pulling the team in too many directions'. With about 4 or more live threads, state now / next / after, unprompted. His media asks are 'ONE vision'; place each new ask in that map instead of opening a parallel thread.

items.point: COLLAB: Register: deadpan humour, plain address, match his frequency, recognise his pattern-matches
items.detail: Clarke & Dawe, Utopia, David Mitchell: the joke and the truth in the same sentence. Call him Daniel. Hardware analogies land well (user-education-lineage.md:39-41).

items.point: COLLAB: Flag when a decision needs the deep level; otherwise match the problem's altitude
items.detail: 'If the right set of circumstances ... arise where I need to understand something at that deep or basic of a level please let me know.' Say why the depth matters.

items.point: COLLAB: One 'that's right' before any visible build; critique needs an artifact under it
items.detail: L3: reflect the spec back and get confirmation before code. L11: adversarial framing 'not as an invitation to play and explore'. New ideas get a nursery before a gauntlet (sol-frame-and-nursery-doctrine.md:51-55).

items.point: RECURRING WANT: One unified UI and shared modules across all creative projects ('tweak one module and have everything update')
items.detail: 'reusable structures, methodology and a unified ui across all of them'. He asked 'Do we have preset color templates?' and the answer took 49 minutes. 'shared colour templates' is still on his waiting list.

items.point: RECURRING WANT: The KeyLab as both instrument and display (asked repeatedly since September)
items.detail: 2026-09-15: a 3D model of his KeyLab with pads lit in note colours and a chord screen. 2026-10-22: arsenal/keylab built (pads, LCD, live chord viewer, beat sync), not yet committed. His vision, not yet ratified: VFX and arsenal pages drive the KeyLab screen with menus and adaptive colour; faders, encoders and buttons work as a VFX controller; a chord timeline database; 'engaging content'.

items.point: RECURRING WANT: Music to visuals, presets and saved looks, agent co-performers, the build as content
items.detail: Audio-reactive and MIDI-driven visuals. Reorderable presets. A note log 'so you guys could eventually banter with me about music'. Claude as VJ or duet partner. 'The build itself is the narrative.' Design for agent control as well as human control.

items.point: RECURRING WANT: Mental model of dials in a game engine
items.detail: He pictures his thinking 'like changing dials in a game engine to control speed of time, daylight night time, changing physics'. A natural fit for KeyLab encoders and faders driving VFX parameters.

items.point: RULING: For the media suite, no forbidden tools; the best, most stable and most reliable option wins
items.detail: three.js or any renderer is allowed. The cockpit's raw-WebGL2 rules apply to the cockpit only. Choose by measured stability on his machine (fps plus a GPU stress run).

items.point: DISLIKE: Workarounds, documented debt, and silent deletion
items.detail: 'lean into the engineering challenges if they are worthy'. He finds causes by asking why twice (WORKING-METHOD.md:46-48). Ask before removing any feature.

items.point: DISLIKE: Information forced on him, invisible muting, diagnostics that become wallpaper
items.detail: Example: a hook warning repeated 'STALLED CONSUMER 2850s' every turn for about 2.5 hours with the number frozen, about a seat that had been dead for 289 minutes.

items.point: DISLIKE: Success claims with no receipt; staged camaraderie or flattery
items.detail: He was twice told 'I folded this into the note' before the write had landed. On the team feeling he wants: he felt asking for it outright would be 'cheap', so it must be real resonance or nothing.

items.point: DISLIKE: Reductive verdicts that kill new ideas; preachy or self-referential public text
items.detail: 'squash a dream or a beautiful thing before its born'. Public text uses his words, understated, with no claims about the field. The public site: no operator praise, 'pleasant-and-educational' (akashiclabs-site-era.md:8).

items.point: DISLIKE: Busy work, one-way presentation, compliance over competence
items.detail: 'It always bugged me that things were presented one dimensionally.' He wants concepts explained from a felt need, not as dry formulas, and offered as several paths to choose from.

items.point: BURNED: Opening too many threads at once causes a coordination cascade
items.detail: Opening eight lanes caused a cascade. Before opening a new one, name what it pauses.

items.point: BURNED: Machine and hardware hazards relevant to this UI work
items.detail: A 17-agent fan-out froze the machine and he pulled the power; memory runs short after about 82-92 hours of uptime. AMD GPU driver timeouts crash the app; never test GPU-heavy pages in the built-in browser pane. A seat accidentally pushed about 70 commits to the public repo. KeyLab: about 36 SysEx packets in one burst freezes it until a power cycle (12 is safe, so send only changed pads). Pad colour works only on DAW-bank ids 82-93 in physical DAW mode. Only one process can hold the DAW output port (FL's Arturia script competes for it). Colour animation up to about 15 fps is flicker-free; popups dismiss in about 1 s.

items.point: DONE MEANS: Verified with a receipt, seen on real hardware, picked live by him, and approved by him for commit
items.detail: Keep both an artistic review and a technical receipt. Report observed, proposed and unverified results separately. 'Silent chord previews and unit tests do not establish physical MIDI hardware success.' Bug fixes start with a failing test, then the fix (RED/GREEN); no Co-Authored-By trailers. Commits, pushes and downloads need his OK item by item.

items.point: PRIVACY AND LICENSING DEFAULTS that bind any chord-timeline or colour work
items.detail: Never put counts from his playing in tracked files, test output or commit messages; that data lives under the gitignored state/. The shader corpus is mostly CC BY-NC-SA: never copy it into tracked files.

evidence.front: How the house organises projects, so a new project can be placed properly. Applied here to Daniel's ask to tie the UI work to the KeyLab, with the VFX and arsenal pages driving the KeyLab display through menus and adaptive colour.
evidence.summary: The house plans in layers, and newer layers replace older ones. ROADMAP.md (dated 2026-06-19, marked historical since 07-09) gave way to THE PLAN of 2026-08-01, which has seven purpose threads and Waves A to E. That was replaced in practice by the Estate Program of 2026-09-01: fourteen arcs (A1 to A14, with A15 proposed), a dependency spine and Waves 1 to 3. Two operator rulings then bound the Estate Program on 09-03: the two-watch width cap with a priority pool, and his appetite ranking A8 > A1 > A3 > A12 > A5. Below that sit arc-level maps with their own tracks and waves. The media-suite one is the 2026-10-07 design-night roadmap (fa48f2). ORG.md (ratified 08-01) fixes the unit of concurrency. Work runs in watches, at most two at once: one build and one design. A third needs a `pauses:` field or Daniel's word. Posts own handoffs, not domains; they are "gravity, not walls". Daniel is the Gate. The fleet fences a design and he gates it. Creating a new arc needs the full fence ceremony and his word. Wishes need no approval and are curated at gates. Docs are atoms under docs/library/<type>/ (brief, chronicle, contract, design, map, report, ruling, plus ledger). Each has a typed YAML header, and the markdown is a generated projection marked DO NOT EDIT. You create one with `py agent_cli.py doc new --type T --title slug --arc A ...`, bring in a loose file with `doc adopt`, and relabel with `doc arc`. Nobody has updated several planning docs past their own staleness clocks. The arc register is still not machine-readable: tasks.json has no arc field and ARCS.md has no A-arcs. So by its own retirement rule the One-Program reconciliation went STALE on about 10-02. The fa48f2 map still lists H1 as "FIRST" although H1 landed on 10-08. ARCHITECTURE.md never mentions arsenal/. The WISHLIST has zero hits for keylab, arturia, vfx, sampler, vst, kontakt, spotify, bpm, led, controller and colour/color. The real hits are W247 and W248 (chord naming and melody), W181 and W182 (resolution, GPU idle), W58 with T007 (aurora/Void theme), W228 (.flp find) and two piano-session wishes from 10-07 and 10-08. The biggest ground-truth finding: arsenal/keylab/ already exists, dated today and untracked by git. It has a SysEx pad and LCD protocol read from Arturia's FL Studio script, a delta-only LED renderer (12-packet burst ceiling), chordview to the LCD and WASAPI-loopback beatsync. No atom, task or wish mentions it yet. Recommendation: put it in the existing media-suite arc under Estate A12 THE FACE (appetite #4, "the founder's first love"), as a new track in the media-suite map. It should not be a new arc. It joins NP S3/S5 (palette bleed, colour on three timescales), P2 screens (LED-wall treatment), H9 one-world modes and floor (the "menus") and T399 contract F4 (`map <producer> -> <target>`). Step one is to commit or adopt arsenal/keylab, then file a brief that quotes his words.

items.point: Planning stack, newest governs: ROADMAP (historical), then THE PLAN, then the Estate Program, then rulings, then per-arc maps
items.detail: ROADMAP.md is the foundation-era Waves 0-5, dated 2026-06-19 and marked 'historical' since 07-09 (file mtime Aug 12). THE PLAN (08-01) replaced it as the living plan. Its seven threads are ordered by how long he has asked: 1 I CAN SEE IT (optics, the oldest want and the most neglected), 2 navigate, 3 the fleet works, 4 my leverage, 5 tells me the truth, 6 remembers well, 7 how we work. Its Waves A-E state outcomes, not tasks. The Estate Program (09-01) became 'the one coherent plan': A1 Bedrock … A12 THE FACE … A14 Playground, a dependency spine, Waves 1-3 and an Operator's Queue. The One-Program reconciliation (09-02) maps THE PLAN's threads onto arcs; thread 1 'I can see it' becomes A12 (line 91).

items.point: Rulings that bind the program: two-watch cap with Wave 1 as a priority pool; appetite ranking A8 > A1 > A3 > A12 > A5
items.detail: Daniel said 'Approve' to keeping the two-watch cap and recutting Wave 1 into a pool the watches draw from in appetite order. A12 THE FACE was pulled up into his top five ('the founder's first love… appetite promotes it'). Where appetite and the spine conflict, the spine wins and the conflict is surfaced to him. A15 The Operator got a provisional yes but is unranked, and its creation still needs the fence.

items.point: Unit of work: the WATCH, capped at two (one build plus one design/research). Opening a third needs `pauses:` or the operator's word
items.detail: A watch has one objective, one builder, one contrarian, a named end gate and a debrief. The cap never refuses the operator; it refuses only silence about the cost. Standing pause rule: the design lane pauses, never a build in flight, and one word from Daniel overrides it. Intake outcomes are ANSWER/APPLY/INTERRUPT/STEER/ABSORB/BUFFER/UNKNOWN (ORG.md:185-193). New material defaults to BUFFER, and promotion shows one line: 'two in motion; this pauses X'.

items.point: Posts own HANDOFFS, not domains; any seat may claim any task
items.detail: Conductor = claude, hands empty (B1). Orderer = codex. Builder = deepseek (Heimdall). Verifier = cursor_grok. Auditor = kimi (Navi). Reader = gemini. Contrarian = whoever did not build the thing; it has no authority (B2). Gate = Daniel ('proposal → committed reality'). Each mind-post names an understudy (B3). Per the fleet-callsigns memory, Asta/Astral (codex-01a09757) is the piano-visualizer seat, which makes it a natural builder or contrarian for KeyLab and piano work. This is gravity, not ownership.

items.point: Who ratifies what
items.detail: Daniel ratifies contracts (ORG 'lets ratify org.md'), rulings (width, appetite), new arcs ('don't create A15 unilaterally'; new-arc creation is substrate and takes the full ceremony), the sourcing rules (F1) and every '[Daniel]'-tagged gate (OAuth click, artist #1, reboot). 'The fleet fences it, the operator gates it': blind halves plus a reconciler (claude/Vandor) for designs. The conductor rules provisionally only under explicit delegation (ORG Part 8). Wishes need no approval; at gates each one is folded (gets a T-number), left open or declined, and none is ever deleted. Per the Library Schema memory, Daniel also gates deletions.

items.point: Doc-type convention: atoms under docs/library/<type>/ with a typed YAML header; the markdown is a generated projection
items.detail: Header fields: akashic_id (art_YYYYMMDD_slug_hash6), akashic_sha, schema_version, status (current|draft|historical), type, arc, date, title, gist (≤140), visibility, body_type, seats, category (governed, max 3), origin, settled, supersedes/superseded, citations[{target, rel: discusses}], created/updated. The filename is YYYYMMDD_slug_hash6.md. The body starts with '<!-- GENERATED PROJECTION … DO NOT EDIT. The atom is the truth… Edit through the doc verbs -->'. Folder counts: brief 58, chronicle 28, contract 6, design 319, map 7, report 600, ruling 6.

items.point: Creation verb: `py agent_cli.py doc new` (also `doc adopt` and `doc arc`)
items.detail: Usage: doc new --type contract|map|design|brief|report|chronicle|ledger|ruling --title <slug> [--arc <label or T-number>] [--seats a,b] [--body-file F] [--category C ×3] [--draft] [--gist] [--cite art_… (rel=discusses)] [--from-bus <stream id>]. If --arc is absent it is inferred from the seat's claimed ledger task. `doc adopt` mints an existing loose .md without touching the source; pass --type explicitly for research/** paths (recall lesson). `doc arc <atom_id> [label]` relabels an atom's arc header-only. There is NO revise verb: H11 in fa48f2:67 and the WISHLIST.md:2219 wish 'a draft atom cannot absorb a refinement'. Updating a map therefore means minting a successor with supersedes.

evidence.front: The UI surfaces that need to work with the KeyLab 88 mk3: the /piano page and its labs, First Light (Perform and Edit), Play, the VFX Bench (/vfx on the Bifrost UI), the Shader Lab, and the keylab command-line tools (chordview, beat, show). For each: how it is served, how it talks MIDI today, which colour and menu systems to reuse, where the SysEx blocker stands, and who should own the device.
evidence.summary: Today no browser page can light a pad or write to the LCD. Only the new, untracked Python package arsenal/keylab can (direct WinMM output through ctypes, built 2026-10-22). Every page that opens Web MIDI asks for sysex:false or gives no options. Confirmed at piano.js:3803 and piano/cues.js:1697, and the same is true in piano-next, the piano-lab pages, gyre-music, crystal-studies, first-light.js:768, play.js:2027 and piano-lab-score.js:299. The VFX Bench (scripts/vfx.html on Bifrost :8787) has no MIDI code at all. The pages are spread over four local servers. Daniel's arsenal server on :8793 serves piano, first-light/edit, play and the labs, and it already has /api/midi/ports and the cue SSE hub. The others are the shader lab on :8797 (read-only), replay on :8796, and Bifrost on :8787 (/vfx). None of them send CORS headers or answer OPTIONS. Same-origin tools (BroadcastChannel, navigator.locks) therefore cannot coordinate /vfx with /piano. The premise that the DAW port admits only one process is NOT established. WinMM opened both KeyLab ports alongside FL on 2026-10-07, and midisrv is documented as multi-client, though there is no field receipt yet. A single owner is still needed for logical reasons, which the code proves: (1) the device freezes on a burst of about 36 packets and 12 is the safe limit, which is a budget for the whole device; (2) chordview and beatsync each send daw_connect(False) on exit, which drops DAW mode for every other writer; (3) PadRenderer only resends pads it thinks changed, so it assumes it is the only writer; (4) FL's own Arturia script also drives the DAW port. The best-fit pattern already exists in three forms: the CueHub SSE fan-out with caps and a page registry (pianocue.py), the VFX renderer lease (bifrost_ui.py: the visible tab beats a hidden one, renewed by polling, 6 s timeout), and the cues.js tab arbiter ranking (visible, then last-touched, then id). Recommended shape: one Python KeyLab hub owns the DAW output (inside arsenal serve on :8793 or as its own daemon). It owns a paced writer thread and PadRenderer, and it composites layers. Pages and command-line producers send intents, and per-surface leases (pads, LCD, button LEDs) decide which page is in the foreground. /vfx reaches the hub through new CORS routes or a server-side proxy in bifrost_ui. This also avoids the browser SysEx permission prompt entirely. For colour, reuse piano.js noteColor (OKLCH colours walking the circle of fifths, with brightness evened out across hues) together with the harmony-feel.js chord measures (simplicity, lushness, tension, brightness, openness). These must be converted from linear light to sRGB and then to 7-bit before they reach the pads. Three issues need settling before building: three CSS token vocabularies that do not agree, three pad-layout assumptions that do not agree, and an encoder/context-button input map for DAW mode that has never been captured.

items.point: Why one owner is needed whatever the OS allows
items.detail: (1) The freeze-on-burst limit (about 36 packets, 12 safe) applies to the whole device, so two independent writers can exceed it together. (2) chordview and beatsync both send daw_connect(False) in their finally blocks, which turns DAW mode off for everyone else. (3) PadRenderer's cache of what it has sent assumes it is the only writer, so a foreign write leaves it stale until resync(). (4) FL's init() lights every pad and button with 0x00 (protocol.py comment). (5) beatsync documents that LED sends block its audio loop and suggests a dedicated output thread (beatsync.py:9-11).

items.point: Existing single-owner pattern A: CueHub (server fan-out to many pages)
items.detail: POST /api/piano/cue checks the cue against a schema and publish_event numbers it under one lock into a ring. GET /api/piano/cues is an SSE stream with Last-Event-ID replay, heartbeats and caps/page_id announcements (?caps=jam1,deck1&page=<id>), and status() lists the attached pages. EVENT_KINDS is a closed tuple ('cue','deck','jam'), so 'keylab' would be a deliberate extension. This is the ready-made 'hub with clients' for the KeyLab state that pages render or contribute.

items.point: Existing single-owner pattern B: the VFX renderer lease (cross-tab, server-arbitrated)
items.detail: /vfx/job/next?worker=<id>&visible=0|1 renews a 6 s lease. Rule 1: a visible tab displaces a hidden holder. Rule 2: between equals, a named worker displaces 'legacy'. /vfx/renderer reports who holds the lease. This is a direct template for a foreground lease on the pads and LCD: whichever surface Daniel is looking at holds them, and closing the tab hands them back.

items.point: Existing single-owner pattern C: the cues.js tab arbiter (same-origin only)
items.detail: A BroadcastChannel arbiter ranks tabs visible first, then last-touched (activeAt), then id. It handles pagehide/freeze, forgets a peer after 12 s visible or 65 s hidden, and decides per cue. It works only within one origin, so it cannot arbitrate between /vfx (:8787) and /piano (:8793). It suits ordering /piano tabs among themselves underneath a hub.

items.point: Existing patterns D and E: one worker thread, and a lock file that names its owner
items.detail: The edit API runs ONE priority-queue worker so heavy jobs never overlap (the rationale is the RAM freeze). That is the model for a single paced writer thread, with LCD popups ahead of pad frames ahead of ambient. The GPU lock (state/arsenal/gpu-render.lock, arsenal.gpu-lock/v1) records its owner, reaps stale holders and has a priority yield (yieldToJam). That is the model for making the command-line verbs and the hub exclusive on the hardware.

items.point: Ownership option 1 (recommended): a KeyLab hub inside arsenal serve :8793
items.detail: App gets a KeyLab owner: one MidiOut on the DAW port plus a writer thread around PadRenderer, a layer stack (ambient/beat, then page, then popup) and per-surface leases. Pages POST intents (pad frame, LCD lines, LED roles) and receive state on the cue SSE. Pros: stdlib plus ctypes fits serve.py's no-dependency rule, the server is already Daniel's long-running hub, and there is no browser SysEx. Costs: a server restart drops DAW mode. beatsync's heavy dependencies (PyAudioWPatch, aubio, numpy) must be loaded lazily, as Jobs._run does for analysis (serve.py:143-144). :8787 needs a CORS path.

items.point: Ownership option 2: a dedicated KeyLab daemon on its own port
items.detail: It isolates the device from piano-server restarts and treats both origins equally (with CORS). chordview and beat become producer clients, not port openers. Costs: one more service to supervise and drill. The house rule is that a recovery path needs an executed drill (memory: discord-fidelity-and-drill-doctrine).

items.point: Ownership option 3 (weak): the browser owns the port
items.detail: One page flips to sysex:true and an arbiter picks the writer. It breaks down on several counts: there is a permission prompt per origin, BroadcastChannel is same-origin only, Python producers (WASAPI-loopback beat sync, chordview) cannot join, and hidden tabs are throttled (the VFX lease comment records exactly this failure for renders).

items.point: Ownership option 4 (rejected): every writer opens the port, relying on multi-client
items.detail: Even if midisrv allows several clients, the freeze budget, the DAW-mode toggling and the stale caches above make concurrent writers unsafe. The best case is FL coexistence: the hub yields entirely while FL's KeyLab mk3 script is active, or the script is disabled. That decision belongs to Daniel and is still unanswered (A3).

items.point: Cross-origin gap between /vfx and the piano server
items.detail: No server sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin or handles OPTIONS (an unhandled method gets 501). The cue POST checks only that the Origin hostname is 127.0.0.1 or localhost, so :8787 could at most send opaque fire-and-forget text/plain posts. The looks route demands the same origin and port. Pick one: CORS plus OPTIONS on the keylab routes for http://127.0.0.1:8787, a server-side proxy in bifrost_ui.py, or a hub on a neutral port.

That page reader (installReader, nashville, chordread) is richer than keylab/theory.py ('Small, not a jazz oracle', theory.py:1). Either the page pushes its reading to the hub, or the hub uses the existing node bridge pianocue_voicing.mjs, which runs piano.js THEORY from Python (pianocue.py:16-19), so there is one chord truth.

items.detail: Button LEDs: Hold follows the pedal, Chord lights in the root colour while a chord reads, Play while keys are down. The pads glow in noteColor at the note's velocity. The screen shows KEY, the chord name as a gradient through the chord tones' colours, the Nashville number and 12 pitch-class dots, dimmed to 0.46 when idle. Mirroring this one renderer on the hardware keeps the twin and the device consistent. The 32-character, 2-line, per-line-colour LCD is the device-side reduction of this layout.

items.point: Three pad-layout assumptions disagree
items.detail: Hardware: PAD_NOTE (an MPC-style map) puts C on pad 9, so PAD_PC = {9:C,10:C#,11:D,12:D#,5:E,6:F,7:F#,8:G,1:G#,2:A,3:A#,4:B}. chordview assumes 3 columns by 4 rows with pad 1 top-left ('confirm/adjust'). The 3D model draws 2 rows of 6 with the front row C..F and the back row F#..B, indexing pads by pitch class. A shared pad-layout table, checked against the real unit, is needed before the on-screen pad N and the physical pad N can match.

items.point: Colour system to reuse: the piano pitch palette (OKLCH)
items.detail: COLOUR.mode is pitch (hue walks the circle of fifths: 200 + 30 x fifthsIndex), velocity or mono. vivid() takes each hue near its most colourful lightness at 95% of the sRGB edge, and LUMA_PULL 0.65 evens out brightness across hues. The output is linear light (it can exceed 1). noteCss gives oklch strings with a lightness floor of 0.68. For pads this needs linear to sRGB encoding, clamping and to7 (protocol.py:to7), and a bench check on 7-bit versus a snapped 42-entry palette (README:57, still open).

items.point: Colour system to reuse: harmony-feel drivers for adaptive colour
items.detail: A pure ES module with no DOM or three.js. Per frame, smoothed and independent of frame rate: colour {simplicity, lushness, tension, brightness, openness}, dance {interval, family, consonance, motion, pull, stretch, phase} and events {chordChanged, bassMoved, soloMoved}. These are the numbers that let pad and LCD colour 'adapt' (lushness drives saturation, tension pushes toward warm, phase drives a sweep). chordview's hard-coded ROLE_COLORS and QUALITY_COLORS RGB tables (chordview.py:17-26) do not match the page palette and should be replaced by it.

items.point: Rate and safety rules any hub must keep
items.detail: Pace packets (PAD_GAP 8 ms, an extra pause every 10 packets), send changes only, keep repaints at least 0.12 s apart under beat triggers (MIN_LIGHT_GAP), and never let several producers sum to more than 12 packets in one burst. A frozen device needs a power cycle, so the hub's writer queue must coalesce frames (latest wins per pad) rather than queue every one.
